title: Looking into the Brain: The Neuroscience Revolution
coreMove: Treat flashbacks as present-tense brain states: check body alarm, language access, and time sense before demanding a clean story from someone in distress.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a patient may be mislabeled evasive when language access is impaired
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use the Rita Fisler PET study to treat lost speech as state information

exampleSpecs.stakes: a demand for written sequence can deepen shame
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Marsha's delayed alarm to explain why time elapsed does not equal integration

exampleSpecs.stakes: a polished edit may erase the very symptom the scene needs to show
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: preserve lost sequence as evidence of traumatic recall rather than smoothing it away

exampleSpecs.audience: peer-support trainers after a rough call
exampleSpecs.stakes: a recruit can be shamed for losing sequence under alarm
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: repair a debrief by asking for state markers before chronology

exampleSpecs.stakes: fluent testimony can be overvalued while fragmented recall is doubted
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: contrast polished narrative with state-based speech loss without claiming scans prove everything

exampleSpecs.stakes: a product can demand narrative before the user has access to words
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: change an intake flow from clean story first to state check first
